evidence.current_assessment: The general finite-game result is a reduction to a Brouwer fixed-point hypothesis; independent compilation is not yet green.

targets.statement: For every finite normal-form game, if the mixed-strategy profile space has the fixed-point property required by the Nash map, then a mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium exists.
targets.goal: Repair and rename the existing candidate so the theorem signature exposes the Brouwer hypothesis, compiles at Lean/Mathlib 4.32.0, and preserves the raw axiom audit.

targets.statement: For the finite-game Nash map formed by adding positive deviation gains and renormalizing, a mixed profile is a fixed point if and only if it is a Nash equilibrium.
targets.goal: Extract the algebraic core from the current Nash candidate into a small axiom-clean Lean module, without invoking a fixed-point existence theorem.

targets.statement: In a finite two-player zero-sum game whose payoff matrix is circulant and skew-symmetric, the uniform mixed profile is a Nash equilibrium.
targets.goal: Formalize the finite matrix game and prove the uniform-equilibrium result by row/column symmetry and zero-sum inequalities.

targets.statement: The point-mass distribution on any pure Nash equilibrium of a finite game is a correlated equilibrium.
targets.goal: Define finite correlated equilibrium incentive constraints and prove the point-mass embedding.

targets.statement: The product joint distribution induced by any mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium of a finite game is a correlated equilibrium.
targets.goal: Prove the implication for a supplied mixed Nash equilibrium; do not claim existence of the Nash premise.

targets.statement: The set of correlated equilibria of a finite game is convex: every convex combination of two correlated equilibria is a correlated equilibrium.
targets.goal: Prove convexity directly from the linear incentive inequalities.

targets.statement: Every finite game has a correlated equilibrium, conditional on the finite mixed-Nash existence theorem used as its premise.
targets.goal: Compose the reviewed Nash existence result with the product-distribution embedding, keeping any fixed-point premise explicit.

targets.statement: Every finite perfect-information extensive-form game with deterministic terminal payoffs has a pure-strategy subgame-perfect equilibrium obtained by backward induction.
targets.goal: Use well-founded recursion on a finite game tree and prove optimality in every subgame.

targets.statement: A finite Bayesian game with a common prior induces a finite normal-form game on contingent plans, and Bayesian Nash equilibria correspond to Nash equilibria of the induced game.
targets.goal: Formalize the finite type/action/prior data and prove the equilibrium-preserving normal-form reduction.

targets.statement: Every finite Bayesian game has a Bayesian Nash equilibrium, conditional on the finite normal-form Nash existence theorem used after the contingent-plan reduction.
targets.goal: Keep the normal-form Nash premise and any Brouwer dependency explicit in the final theorem signature.

targets.statement: Every strict Nash equilibrium of a finite normal-form game is trembling-hand perfect.
targets.goal: Formalize completely mixed trembles and the limiting definition, then prove robustness of strict best responses.

targets.statement: In every finite extensive-form game with perfect recall, each mixed strategy has an outcome-equivalent behavioral strategy and conversely.
targets.goal: Treat this as a later theorem after information sets, realization probabilities, and perfect recall have independent verified definitions.

targets.statement: For a finite repeated game, if every player's external regret after T rounds is at most epsilon times T, then the empirical distribution of joint play is an epsilon-coarse-correlated equilibrium.
targets.goal: Prove the finite-time averaging identity directly from the external-regret inequalities.

targets.statement: For losses in [0,1], the Hedge exponential-weights algorithm with learning rate eta > 0 has external regret at most log(n)/eta + eta*T/8.
targets.goal: Pin the precise update and finite-horizon bound before composing it with the coarse-correlated-equilibrium theorem.

targets.statement: Every solution of finite-population replicator dynamics that starts in the probability simplex remains in the simplex throughout its interval of existence.
targets.goal: Separate the tangency/nonnegativity argument from the ODE existence dependency.

targets.statement: For a finite game with rational payoffs and a rational mixed profile, whether the profile is a Nash equilibrium is decidable by finitely many exact payoff inequalities.
targets.goal: Give an executable decision procedure and prove it equivalent to the finite best-response definition.

targets.statement: Every rational bimatrix profile returned by a support-enumeration solver satisfies the Nash equilibrium inequalities.
targets.goal: Formalize soundness before completeness or complexity claims.

targets.statement: Computing a Nash equilibrium of a finite two-player bimatrix game is PPAD-complete under a precisely specified finite encoding and reduction notion.
targets.goal: Start with a statement-level formalization; do not claim the hardness reduction until the encoding and total-search framework are independently verified.

targets.statement: In a finite single-item second-price auction with deterministic tie-breaking and quasilinear utilities, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy.
targets.goal: Pin tie-breaking and utility conventions, then prove truthfulness by cases on the highest competing bid.

targets.statement: For a finite outcome space and quasilinear agents, the VCG allocation rule with Clarke-pivot payments is dominant-strategy incentive compatible.
targets.goal: Generalize only after the second-price special case and finite argmax lemmas verify.

targets.statement: A game with nonempty compact convex strategy sets and continuous payoffs that are quasiconcave in each player's own strategy has a Nash equilibrium, assuming the required Kakutani fixed-point theorem.
targets.goal: Formalize the best-response correspondence and prove the reduction while leaving the Kakutani premise explicit.

targets.statement: State Glicksberg's equilibrium-existence theorem for compact strategy spaces and continuous payoffs with all topological and measurability hypotheses explicit.
targets.goal: Statement-level target only until the finite-dimensional continuous-game layer and fixed-point firewall are verified.
